title: Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
statement:
The string `s` is made of lowercase English letters and the brackets `'('` and `')'`. Delete as few brackets as possible (from any positions; letters are never deleted) so that what remains is a valid parentheses string, and return the remaining string. When several strings can be reached with the fewest deletions, return any one of them.

A string is valid when it is empty or contains only letters, when it is two valid strings written one after the other, or when it is a valid string wrapped in one `'('` and one `')'`. Equivalently, every `')'` closes an earlier unmatched `'('` and no `'('` is left unmatched.
constraints: s[i] is '(', ')' or a lowercase English letter
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every subset of brackets to delete would be exponential. Instead, notice which brackets are hopeless. Scanning left to right with a stack of unmatched `'('` positions, a `')'` that arrives when the stack is empty can never be matched, so it must go. When the scan ends, every `'('` still on the stack has no partner, so it must go too. Every other bracket is part of a matched pair, so these forced deletions are also the fewest possible.

## Approach

1. Split `s` into `chars` so single characters can be blanked out.
2. Walk the indices `i`. Push the index of each `'('` onto `stack`.
3. For a `')'`, pop its partner if `stack` has one; otherwise blank `chars[i]`.
4. After the scan, blank every index still on `stack`.
5. Join `chars` back into a string.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "lee(t(c)o)de)"`. The `'('` at index 3 is pushed, then the one at index 5: `stack = [3, 5]`. The `')'` at index 7 pops 5, and the `')'` at index 9 pops 3. The `')'` at index 12 finds the stack empty, so `chars[12]` is blanked. Nothing is left on the stack, so the result is `"lee(t(c)o)de"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one scan, then at most n pops.
- Space: O(n) for `chars` and `stack`.

## Pitfalls

- Store indices on the stack, not characters, so leftover `'('` can be found and removed.
- Do not stop after the left-to-right pass: unmatched `'('` only show up at the end.
- Blank removed slots instead of splicing them out, which would shift the stored indices and cost O(n) per removal.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `chars` | the characters of `s`, with removed brackets set to `''` |
| `stack` | indices of `'('` still waiting for a partner |
| `i` | the index being scanned |

narration.2: Split the string into characters so single positions can be blanked out.
narration.3: The stack holds the indices of '(' that have not been matched yet.
narration.4: Scan the string from left to right.
narration.5: An opening bracket may be matched later...
narration.7: A closing bracket needs an unmatched '(' before it.
narration.8: Is there an open bracket waiting?
narration.9: Yes: they form a pair, so the '(' is no longer waiting.
narration.11: No: this ')' can never be matched, so delete it.
narration.15: Any '(' still on the stack never found a partner.
narration.18: Glue the kept characters back into the answer.
